author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: Add the data collector with logging <address> (UDP 514, TCP 1470 or TLS 6514) and include-auditable-events, so the accounting log goes too. Event log lines (Event|<event ID>|LOG_<severity>|<module role>|<module ID>|<message>) are read by event ID, from HPE's AOS-CX Event Log Message Reference. To Auth: SSH, Telnet, console and REST sign-ins, sign-outs and failures (5209 to 5211, 5215, 5216, 5220 to 5222, 12904 to 12906, 13001 to 13003, 13005, 4655 to 4657, 4662, and REST's 4601 and 4602), account lockouts (4707), and 802.1X and MAC authentication results (10528, 10529, 10531, 10532) with the client MAC, port and RADIUS server in event_metadata; MAC authentication uses the MAC as the user name. A REST sign-in can log both 4602 and 4655. To Management Event: user, password and configuration changes, REST changes, SSH server and key changes, remote logging changes and a cleared security log (the IDs are in the parser), with the event ID, the user who acted and the message; and accounting lines in the AOS-CX format, the default from 10.11, with the command, user, address, session and result. Other events, such as loop protect and port security, stay generic. The time is the header's RFC 3339 time, with the switch's offset. How sure this is: HPE documents the event body, every event message and one accounting line, but not the syslog framing. The RFC 5424 header in the samples (<190>1 <time> <host> <app> <pid> - -) and app names such as log-proxyd come from third-party test data, so the parser reads an RFC 5424 header or a <time> <host> <app>[<pid>]: header and keys on event IDs, never app names. HPE's one accounting example is a CLI command; REST commands and failures aren't documented, and the native Linux accounting format (logging accounting-format-native) isn't read. Samples are made up from HPE's message texts. Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-16 (165 of 165 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there. Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (165 of 165 fields, each line taken in 5 of 5 runs). No built-in parser claimed these lines.
